Priya (sec-eng): Running into a cross-account kms:Decrypt AccessDenied from a Lambda in account B that assumes role InfraCrossAccountRole in account A. Stacktrace: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::222333444:assumed-role/InfraCrossAccountRole/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-ef01`

Ben (infra): @Priya can you paste the key policy + the IAM role trust/policy? most issues are either key policy missing the principal or an encryption-context mismatch.

Priya (sec-eng): Pasting snippets (redacted):

Key policy (kms key in account A):
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAccountARoot",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Trust policy on role in account A that the Lambda in account B assumes (account B id = 222333444):

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222333444:role/LambdaExecutionRole"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
  }]
}

Role inline policy (attached to InfraCrossAccountRole): `{"Statement":[{"Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Effect":"Allow","Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-ef01"}]}`

CloudTrail snippet shows `kms:Decrypt` call with encryptionContext {"purpose":"envelope"}.

Alice (platform): Two quick things: 1) Key policy currently only allows the root of account A. That does NOT automatically grant permissions to assumed roles or principals from other accounts. You need an explicit statement that allows the cross-account principal (or the role ARN) to use the key for Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. 2) If the key was used to GenerateDataKey in account A and a grant was used, grants expire/require grant tokens in some flows.

Ben (infra): Also verify encryption context — Decrypt requires the exact same encryption context used during Encrypt/GenerateDataKey (key names, capitalization). If the Lambda in account B sets a different context, KMS will deny even if perms are correct.

Priya (sec-eng): I tried `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/InfraCrossAccountRole --role-session-name t1` from account B and then ran:

aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin \
  --region us-west-2 \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-ef01 \
  --encryption-context purpose=envelope

Result: `An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt`

Ben (infra): Ok that rules out lambda iam policy. Two possibilities left: key policy lacks the assumed-role principal, or the key uses a grant-only configuration (rare). Show full kms:key policy allowing cross-account principal like this:

{
  "Sid":"AllowCrossAccountDecrypt",
  "Effect":"Allow",
  "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::222333444:role/LambdaExecutionRole"},
  "Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource":"*"
}

Note: Principal may need to be the assumed role ARN `arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/InfraCrossAccountRole/*` depending on how AWS evaluates it. Safer to allow the role ARN in account A and the concrete principal in account B.

Alice (platform): Another common trap: are you using a grant instead of key policy permissions? Grants created by CreateGrant can be limited; if the grant was created in account A for a specific principal it might not apply to the assumed role session. Check `aws kms list-grants --key-id ...` and `aws kms list-grants --key-id ... --grantee-principal arn:aws:sts::222333444:assumed-role/InfraCrossAccountRole/session`

Priya (sec-eng): I ran `aws kms list-grants --key-id ...` — there are no active grants. So it's key policy. I updated a test key policy to include this statement:

{
  "Sid":"CrossAccountLambda",
  "Effect":"Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": [
    "arn:aws:iam::222333444:role/LambdaExecutionRole",
    "arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/InfraCrossAccountRole"
  ]},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}

Tried decrypt again with assume-role creds — still AccessDenied.

Ben (infra): Hmm. Did you attach a Condition in the key policy like `aws:PrincipalArn` or `aws:SourceVpc`? Also CloudTrail for the failed Decrypt will show the principal used (STS ARN). Post that exact principal string.

Priya (sec-eng): CloudTrail shows `userIdentity.arn = arn:aws:sts::222333444:assumed-role/LambdaExecutionRole/i-1234` when the Lambda runs in account B, but when I assume the InfraCrossAccountRole in account A (manual CLI test) CloudTrail shows `arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/InfraCrossAccountRole/t1`. So the actual principal in the failing Decrypt is the latter (account A assumed-role). Key policy allows `arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/InfraCrossAccountRole` but not the assumed-role arn.

Alice (platform): Right — IAM role vs assumed-role ARN difference matters. In key policy Principals should be the IAM role (not the assumed-role STS ARN). But KMS substitution rules sometimes require the kms policy to allow the account or to use `AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333:root"` with a condition limiting to `aws:PrincipalArn` to the role. Example condition approach:

{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:root"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalArn":"arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/InfraCrossAccountRole"}}
}

That lets the account root act but constrains to the role principal.

Ben (infra): Also ensure there aren't any deny statements higher precedence. `kms:*` denies or SCPs from organizations can block. Check org SCPs and service control policies.

Priya (sec-eng): No SCP denies. I removed the restrictive root-only statement and added the AllowCrossAccountDecrypt principal for the role ARN and also added the Condition matching aws:PrincipalArn to the assumed-role path. Then re-ran decrypt with the assumed-role CLI creds — success `Plaintext` returned. :tada:

Priya (sec-eng): Root cause summary I think: key policy originally only allowed account root (insufficient granularity) and when the role was assumed the STS ARN didn't match. Fix options were: add explicit role principal, or allow account root + condition on aws:PrincipalArn, or create a grant.

Ben (infra): Nice. For production please ensure we add narrow scoped actions (Decrypt + GenerateDataKey) and restrict Resource and encryption context if appropriate, and document the change in the KMS config PR. Also add an alert if future Decrypt denials spike.

infra-bot: deploy noted for key-policy update (PR #4823) by Priya — scheduled 03:30 UTC.

Priya (sec-eng): I'll open the PR now with the policy change + justification + test steps. Thanks for the help! :heart:
